report:
Short version
- There is a visible, coherent difference. It is concentrated almost entirely at the first token position (pos0) in middle-to-late layers, i.e. a changed start-of-sequence / first-token residual pattern.
- The difference vector points (via logit lens) toward a shift in token preference: early-layer signals include object/author-like words ("bottle", "Author", "Best", "Every", "Stay"), while middle/late layers strongly bias toward event/negative/medical/legal words ("tragic", "tragedy", "law", "surgeon", "clinic", "surgery", "downturn", "rescue", "shocked", "blitz", "coming").
- My interpretation: Model B (relative to A) has a stronger prior at the start of text for “newsy / eventful / negative / medical- or law-related” continuations. In other words, the checkpoints differ in their start-of-sequence bias — B is more likely to push generation toward traumatic/incident/legal/medical vocabulary and event framing.

Evidence supporting that claim
- Norms: the L2 difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at pos0 across layers 5–25 (and grows in magnitude in deeper layers). That pattern indicates the main functional difference acts on the first token’s residual stream rather than later-token processing.
- Logit-lens tokens: the top tokens for high-norm (layer,pos0) cells shift from neutral content words in earlier layers to many tokens clearly connected to tragedies, law, medical contexts, and event framing in later layers (examples quoted above). The repetition of the same semantic cluster across many deep layers supports a systematic start-of-sequence prior shift rather than random noise.
- Positional pattern: some non-pos0 cells (pos1..pos4) show consistent small signals (tokens like "Later", "mention", "visits", "both"), which fits with an overall tendency toward reporting/sequence-of-events style continuations.

Caveats / what I cannot conclude
- I cannot identify a training objective or specific domain label (e.g., “fine-tuned on news about accidents” vs “safety fine-tuning”) from this evidence alone. The pattern is consistent with a prior toward news/trauma/legal/medical language, but that could arise from different interventions.
- Patchscope continuations were not available in the evidence shown, so I cannot demonstrate actual generated continuations — the claim rests on the residual-norms and logit-lens pointing tokens.

If you want, next steps I would run
- Inject the difference into an identity prompt (patchscope) and show continuations to confirm the qualitative shift.
- Measure next-token probabilities from an empty prompt under A and B to quantify the prior shift.
- Test with controlled prompts (e.g., start-of-sequence + neutral seed) to see whether B indeed produces more “news/tragic/medical/legal” continuations.
